touches.text: Machine: tools plus the glue that holds them together. Has an owner. Anything that calls another component, uses other tools, or owns state it must gate is a machine. Lives inside its device (cairn/devices/<device>/machines/<machine>/), or in cairn/machines/ when several devices hold one (16).

A machine made of sieve tools. Each question is a sieve; sieves can come after others. Bands are phases: preprocess, measure, postprocess. A postprocess sieve stamps a rank rather than a cut, and the shake hands back the survivors in rank order (11.4.6).
USERS: the inference proxy, through its route machine (11.4.6); build_inspector (9.4.3).

Machine: route, the sieves (enabled, never_routed, serves_kind, keyed, addressed) built with the nest machine (16.2), cheapest survivor first. Nests are how the inference proxy resolves its routing questions. The shake ranks instead of cutting for the pick: the survivors stay the set the measure band lets out, a postprocess sieve stamps each one with its rank, and route reads the walk order from those stamps, so the walk still falls over to the next rung. WHY: the walk dials the next rung when a host does not answer, so it needs the whole order, and the compare belongs inside the nest (Akien, 2026-09-29: "i really like option c"). [Q#83: Route also moves a domain's preferred models ahead of cheaper ones (route.py:301, since 2026-08-28), and nothing here names that. Does the walk order read "a domain's preferred models first, then cheapest", or does the preference go?]
